summary: Takudo Ishikawa works in Buddhist studies. He held posts as a researcher at the Jodo Shu Research Institute, attested in 2005, and as a specially appointed full-time lecturer at Taisho University, attested in 2015.

Takushu Sugimoto is an Indologist, archaeologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD from Tohoku University, where he studied under Ensho Kanakura and Hakuyu Hadano. He was a professor at Kanazawa University, Komazawa University, and Kinjo University.

Tan Chung was a scholar of sinology, history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Professor of Chinese at the University of Delhi (circa 1964–1978) and Head of Chinese and Japanese Studies at Jawaharlal Nehru University (circa 1978–1994).

Tansen Sen works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He studied at Peking University under Yinzeng Geng and Xianlin Ji, earned a PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Victor H. Mair, and served at Baruch College.

Tao Jiang is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at Temple University under Shigenori Nagatomo and was attested in 2011 as an Associate Professor in the Department of Religion at Rutgers University.
Tao Jin is a scholar of sinology and religious studies who earned a PhD from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in 2008 under the supervision of Alexander L. Mayer.
Tao Pan is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He earned a BA from Fudan University in 2010 and received a Magister Artium from Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich.

Tarab Tulku was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a curator at the Royal Danish Library from circa 1969 to 1998 and held a post at the University of Copenhagen from circa 1970 to 1998.

Tarif Khalidi is an Arab historian and scholar of religion who studied at University College, Oxford, and the University of Chicago. He held positions at the American University of Beirut (circa 1970–1996) and the University of Cambridge (circa 1996–2007).

Tarthang Tulku is a Buddhist, Tibetology, and philosophy figure who studied under Jamyang Khyentse Chokyi Lodro. He founded the Nyingma Institute, served as its Head and Head Lama, and was Head Lama at Tibetan Nyingma Meditation Center.

Tashi Tsering is a scholar of Tibetology, history, and linguistics. He founded and directed the Amnye Machen Institute, worked as a Research Officer at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives, and was a professor at CIHTS.

Tatiana Oranskaia is an Indologist and linguist. She studied at Saint Petersburg State University from circa 1967 to 1973 and served as a professor at the University of Hamburg from circa 2002 to 2016.

Tatsugen Sato was a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He served as assistant professor and then professor at Komazawa University between circa 1971 and 1995, and also taught at Tokai University and Ryukoku University.
Tatsuhiro Saito is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He studied under Kenyu Mitomo and founded the Nikaya Buddhism Thought Study Group.
Tatsuo Nishida was a linguist, Tibetologist, and sinologist. He studied at Kyoto University from circa 1948 to 1951 and later served as a professor there, attested in 1996.

Tavivat Puntarigvivat works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He earned an MA at the University of Hawaii, directed research at World Buddhist University, chaired comparative religion at Mahidol University, and conducted Zen research at Kyoto University.
Tej Ram Sharma is an Indologist and historian who completed a doctoral thesis at Banaras Hindu University in 1968 and was attested at Himachal Pradesh University in 1978.

Tensei Kitabatake was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (circa 1948–1953) and later served as a professor there (circa 1977–1997). He also held posts at Otani, Gifu Shotoku Gakuen, Kyoto Women's, and Tenri universities.
Tenshin Tanouye was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under the traditional teacher Sogen Omori and founded Chozen-ji.
Tenzin is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed a Master of Philosophy degree at the University of Oslo, attested in 2008, under supervisor Hanna Havnevik.
